title: Easy enough
body:

Note 1: to move a task between folders: open the task to be moved, near top of left side of task, click the down arrow, select the destination folder. Done.

title: Just so helpful!
body:
I use this app on a near daily basis. I have the type of personality that likes to tick off the things I have done and this gives me that; but, more than that, it really helps me organise my days and various events. In this way, I can quietly think through all the elements of a task, order them, and then check them off as I am moving to completion.

As an older person, I appreciate being able to externalise the things I need to do, as it helps me retain a sense of control over household and other matters.

I also have left some tasks as permanent lists - like ‘packing to go away’ - and since doing that, I have never left a phone cable or toothbrush behind!

I highly recommend this app - easy to use, and just so helpful.

title: Kanban View?
body:
Hi Google Tasks,

I’d love to see an update to Google Tasks that introduces a Kanban-style view. The current list format works, but a visual board layout—like columns for “To Do,” “In Progress,” and “Done”—would make task management way more intuitive and efficient. It would help a lot of users organize tasks more dynamically, especially for project-based workflows.

Please consider adding this as an option or view mode. It’d bring Google Tasks in line with modern productivity tools and honestly, it’s long overdue.

Thanks for considering this update!

title: Somewhat helpful but maybe a little too simple
body:
The integration of the tasks into mail and the calendar is helpful and the task list works well on a very basic level. A few additional features would make it genuinely helpful:

1. Replace the scrolling time options (iPhone) when setting a time for a reminder with the ability to simply type in the time. This would be much easier and faster.

2. Swipe left on a reminder to snooze it. Provide the options to snooze it until another day/time similar to the snooze function in Mail.

3. Sub-tasks need to appear as sub tasks, not in a separate list. On iPhone it’s impossible to see that tasks have sub-tasks which means they can be missed. Additionally, when viewing tasks by date the sub-tasks show up in the list at the bottom totally out of context. This is unnecessary and annoying.

4. Ability to share task lists with other users in one’s organisation would be helpful.

5. Ability to move tasks from one list to another on iPhone is necessary.

author: richkenn

title: Calendar and Tasks apps don’t sync well in phone
body: The app has good potential but it needs to be linked with the Google Calendar. This function works well on a computer but the apps barely speak to each other on a phone. Personally it feels like the Google productivity series of tools lack a central platform (especially a mobile one since I assume most people would manage their time when they are in transit) where I can manage all my events and tasks, or could I be missing something?
author: VB Wong

title: Something so simple yet effective!!
body:
Google tasks is the only tasks app I have found that ticks most of my boxes whilst not having any deal-breaking features and without a subscription plan.

Google tasks allows me to organise my daily routine and tasks that I have to accomplish, while it does lack some key features such as repeating tasks, they can be worked around by unticking tasks and placing them back into the list (with the recent update, my checked sub lists finally go back to their parent. THANK YOU GOOGLE.)

More support with google calendar and notes would be appreciated, as tasks don’t seem to sync with the Calender.. 

All in all, I know Tasks is somewhat primitive compared to other to-do apps, but is the only app that doesn’t force a subscription for excessive usage and plus, is constantly being updated, I can only hope for the best.

title: Good start
body: A very simple tasks app. I wish that it was integrated w/ the calendar app, so i could drag and drop tasks into available time slots, and check them off all through the calendar. I also wish the tasks could be added to a calendar group (so they would be different colours, as I’m a visual thinker). The app is a good start, but it needs to be integrated w/ other Google tools.
author: CarloscatMargodog

title: Almost ticking all the boxes!
body: I’ve been waiting for a dedicated Tasks app from Google. This app functions well and the recent update has included some much needed features such as due ‘time’ (but it would be great if it were visible on the task list!) and repeating tasks. It still needs to be integrated with Calendar, but I wonder if this is about to happen noting the prompt to import existing Reminders into Tasks. I need to be able to add an image in notes, not just text. I would love to be able to share tasks and/or whole lists, eg with my husband, then I could consider using it for our grocery shopping list!

author: andrewleehorton

title: A below average task manager
body:
A lacklustre app from Google. It’s functionality is basic and in my opinion lacks some fundamental features you’d have thought would’ve been essential to a decent task manager’s minimal viable product.

I’ll continue to use apps like Wunderlist until this has features like:

- Ability to star/prioritise tasks
- Ability to share lists with other users
- Ability to assign tasks to others
- Ability to set task reminder notifications 
- Ability to attach files/Google Drive files
- Ability to repeat tasks
author: Nathan Bugeja

title: Super awesome idea... but...
body:
Google. Please. For the love of everything that is holy... PLEASE make this app more powerful.
Integration with Google Assistant. Adding an actual time for the ‘task’ to go off should’ve been baseline as well.
Adding a photo to said task would be amazing. That would be the cherry on the cake.

I was ecstatic when I heard about this app and finally thought we’d have a powerful altogether reminders app made by the almighty Google!

But this is such a mess of a situation.

I’m so disappointed. 
Not mad. 
Disappointed.

Please heed these cries, Google. I love you.
author: fearkite

title: Finally!
body:
I use a lot of Goole tools, including tasks as it has an unobtrusive integration with my email workflow.

My greatest complaint has been that the Tasks functionality has never ventured beyond the desktop.

Finally my todo lists can integrate with my phone cleanly. 

I know that Keep does a lot of this and the new ‘Inbox” tries to do tasks as well, but there is an elegant simplicity in just having a list of tasks. 

For a lot of folks, like myself, don’t need or want a lot of bells and whistles - we just need a list that syncs with our desktops. 

This is it. Simplicity itself. 

My only ask to make it better would be to allow the Gmail app to be able to assign a task from an email. Just like on the desktop. That would make this perfect for all time. If you had that, I’d have given 5-stars.
author: MUPC

title: Bare-bones but nice UX and UI
body: Will appeal to minimalists who don't need a lot of features like timed task reminders or repeating tasks. It's lacking integration with Google calendar which seems like a no-brainer, and also lacking integration with Google Reminders in Inbox. It feels like there are 50 different ways you can create tasks and reminders in Google's ecosystem, none of them talk to each other. Google just needs a simple way to take notes (Keep is great) and a simple way to make tasks with reminders that are accessible from Gmail and Calendar - hopefully this app will be the answer to this conundrum.
